report.summary: Chunk 2 of 6: git stamp helpers, narrative parsing, and markdown rendering up to block dispatch.
risks: _head | medium | Uses string splitting to extract branch name; may fail on unusual ref formats. | Inspect ref format edge cases.
_dirty | low | subprocess timeout 30s may hang on large repos. | Consider async or timeout handling.
_untracked | low | Uses subprocess with timeout; may fail silently. | Ensure error handling covers all cases.
_inline | low | Inline code and bold regexes may overlap or be nested; order matters. | Test with nested markup.
_md_blocks | medium | Table parsing assumes separator rows contain only '-', ':', spaces; may misparse. | Test with complex tables.
_md_blocks | low | List parsing uses indentation heuristic; may break on mixed list types. | Test nested lists.

claims.text: How many of the files the SCANNER read are unknown to git.
claims.why: SCANNER is not defined in this chunk; the claim refers to external context.

claims.text: git status --porcelain answers 'what changed among the things git is watching'. It is silent about a file excluded via .git/info/exclude, a global core.excludesfile or assume-unchanged
claims.why: The claim describes git behavior not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: ls-files what is TRACKED, and subtracting, is the only version of this claim that is verified rather than assumed.
claims.why: The function does run git ls-files -z and subtracts tracked from scanned.

claims.text: Escape FIRST, then apply inline markup. Order is the whole safety argument: after escaping there is no < left in the string, so every tag in the result is one this function put there.
claims.why: The code first calls esc(text) (HTML escape), then substitutes code and bold patterns.

claims.text: The narrative file is hand-written but the prose inside it was gathered by agents, and agent-authored text is untrusted input.
claims.why: The origin of the narrative file is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: A section is addressed by an explicit {#key} suffix on its heading rather than by matching its wording, so the prose can be retitled, rewritten or translated without silently detaching itself from the slot it renders into.
claims.why: The function uses _SECTION_KEY_RE to extract key from heading, and uses that key for addressing.

claims.text: A heading with no key still renders -- under 'further narrative' -- because dropping a section somebody wrote is the one behaviour this file must never have.
claims.why: If no key found, key is set to 'extra-' + slug of heading, ensuring it is not dropped.

observations.what: _resolve_ref function appears to read a git ref file; its implementation is partially visible (line 281-285).
_head function uses string splitting to extract branch name; may not handle all ref formats correctly.
_dirty function uses subprocess with timeout 30s; may hang on large repos.
_untracked function uses subprocess to run git ls-files; error handling returns -1 on failure.
Narrative dataclass uses NARRATIVE_SECTIONS which is not defined in this chunk.
parse_narrative uses _SECTION_KEY_RE and _slug which are not defined in this chunk.
_inline function uses esc() which is not defined in this chunk.
_md_blocks table parsing assumes separator rows contain only '-', ':', spaces; may misparse.
_md_blocks list parsing uses indentation heuristic; may break on mixed list types.
_render_md function is incomplete; only shown up to table handling.
